parent: Independent broad-confirmation breakout ownership: market_window=120, recovery_breadth=0.75, stop_atr=3.5, entry_window=40, entry_cap=0.7.
hypothesis: A short breakout during a prolonged decline can still lie below its longer structural trend. Such entries caused repeated losses after the initial technology rally. Require the prospective holding itself to be above a slower causal mean, while allowing faster closing trend damage to invalidate an already-owned position before the wide true-range trail.
entry: Retain the parent's fresh breakout, broad-entry gate and cash constraints, and require close above the entry_mean simple moving average, using expanding observed history after at least ten observations. No retrospective peak dates or security identifiers.
exit: Close below the causal exit_mean exponential mean times (1-exit_band) is additional evidence to liquidate, only for actual confirmed units with a fresh quote. Existing non-widening ownership stop and entry-cost stop retain priority; liquidation intent persists through blocked fills. The next-session engine remains unchanged. Existing economic units are never trimmed just because their market weights grow.
selection_objective: mean(log(wealth / matched buy_hold wealth) - 0.75 * max_drawdown - 0.002 * max(0, orders_per_year - 20))
evidence: Preserve all twelve configurations and all failed predecessors. Hash the ownership, broad-entry and additional rule implementations. Prefix equality and fresh-quote exit behavior are necessary checks. Full-period evaluation remains retrospective. No change to frozen accounting, fees, data, liquidity or economic targets.
